newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statfjord, Gullfaks, Snorre oilfields curb output.
newsitem.headline: Statfjord, Gullfaks, Snorre oilfields curb output.

text.p: Oil production at the North Sea Statfjord, Gullfaks and Snorre platforms was down to roughly one third of normal output on Thursday because of stormy weather preventing offshore loadings, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said.
Statfjord and Snorre reduced output on Tuesday and Wednesday because of disruptions to loadings and burgeoning storage and were followed early on Thursday by Gullfaks.

"The whole Statfjord complex plus Snorre are now producing 330,000 barrels per day against a normal output of 860,000 bpd, or 40 percent of normal production," Statoil spokesman Lars Gunnar Dahle said.
"Gullfaks cut production to 20 percent early this morning and is now pumping 95,000 bpd against normal 470,000 bpd," he said.
"Full production at all these fields is 1.33 milion bpd, but now it is down to 425,000 bpd, or 32 percent of normal," Dahle said.
"Waves now raise to a maximum eight metres," he said. "The weather outlook is bad. It is going to get worse before it gets better. We hope, however, that loadings can resume on Saturday."
The maximium permitted wave height for shuttle tankers to moor to offshore loading buoys is 4.5 metres.
Pumping was halted at Statfjord A at midnight on Tuesday. Snorre, which feeds crude to Statfjord A for processing and loading, was closed at the same time.
Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrels per day (bpd) and processes oil from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre development.
